title: Composition, refinement, and base localization of etale descent
statement: For each quasi-separated scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F(T)$ be the category whose objects are finitely presented chartwise etale algebraic spaces $X\to T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] and whose arrows are all maps over $T$. Finite presentation means local finite presentation on charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compactness on affine scheme tests, and quasi-compact relative diagonal. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. For $q:T'\to T$, an object of $\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal F}(q)$ is $X'\in\mathcal F(T')$ with an isomorphism between its two pullbacks to $T'\times_TT'$, identity on the diagonal and satisfying the triple-product cocycle. Arrows commute with these isomorphisms. Call $q$ a universal $\mathcal F$-descent morphism if the canonical functor $\mathcal F(V)\to\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal F}(T'\times_TV\to V)$ is fully faithful for every quasi-separated scheme $V\to T$; call it universal effective descent if each such functor is an equivalence. Then: (i) the composite of two universal effective descent morphisms is universal effective descent; (ii) if $X\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{b}T$ has universally effective composite $ba$, then $b$ is universal effective descent; (iii) suppose $q:T'\to T$ is universal descent and $g:V\to T$ is universal effective descent. A datum for $q$ is effective if its pullback along $g$ is effective. These assertions include specified compatible realization isomorphisms, not just isomorphism classes.

source.place: Propositions (5.6) and (5.7), printed p.19, for the fibre category E_qc of Notation (5.1), identified with finitely presented etale spaces by Remark (5.2). Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Use sheaf pullbacks from [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. All bases stay quasi-separated: for quasi-separated $T'\to T\leftarrow V$, the map $T'\to T$ is quasi-separated, so its base change $T'\times_TV\to V$ is quasi-separated and $T'\times_TV$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1)-(3); hence $T'\times_TT'$, triple products and all base changes used below are again quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The space pullbacks preserve chartwise etaleness by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], hence local finite presentation on scheme charts by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The quasi-compactness of both the structural map and its relative diagonal is preserved by base change by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]; the new relative diagonal is the pullback of the old one. Thus these pullbacks stay in $\mathcal F$. Reassociation of compatible tuples gives the pullback comparison isomorphisms, satisfying the unit and associativity identities. We can apply the pseudofunctor lemma below to this $\mathcal F$. Work throughout with arbitrary additional quasi-separated scheme base changes, so every use of a universal hypothesis is legitimate.

source.place: Notation (5.1), Remark (5.2), printed pp.17-18; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03FU and spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03HF

proof.text: Prove (ii) first. Write $K_b:\mathcal F(T)\to\operatorname{Desc}(b)$ and $R=a^*$. Since $ba$ is universal effective descent, it is universal descent. By [lem-sfb-descent-data-refinement-hom], $R$ is fully faithful and $RK_b\cong K_{ba}$. For $C,D\in\mathcal F(T)$ the map on Hom sets for $RK_b$ is bijective, as is the map induced by $R$; hence the map for $K_b$ is bijective. Given a $b$-datum $D$, choose $C$ and a specified isomorphism $K_{ba}C\cong RD$. Fullness of $R$ lifts this isomorphism and its inverse to arrows $K_bC\rightleftarrows D$; faithfulness gives their inverse identities. Thus $K_b$ is an equivalence. This applies after every base change, proving the universal assertion and preserving the specified realization comparison.

For (iii), write the datum as $(A,\alpha)$ on $T'$ and choose a realization $B\in\mathcal F(V)$ and compatible isomorphism $\beta:B|_{T'\times_TV}\xrightarrow{\sim}A|_{T'\times_TV}$. Put $V_n=V\times_T\cdots\times_TV$ ($n$ factors), $W_n=T'\times_TV_n$. On $W_2$, the two pullbacks $\beta_1,\beta_2$ have the same target $A|_{W_2}$. Set $\delta=\beta_2^{-1}\beta_1:B_1|_{W_2}\to B_2|_{W_2}$. This is an arrow between the canonical descent data for $W_2\to V_2$: on $T'\times_TT'\times_TV_2$, compatibility of each $\beta_i$ with $\alpha$ reads $\alpha\beta_i^{(1)}=\beta_i^{(2)}$, whence $\delta^{(2)}=(\beta_2^{(2)})^{-1}\beta_1^{(2)}=(\beta_2^{(1)})^{-1}\beta_1^{(1)}=\delta^{(1)}$ under the canonical identifications. Full faithfulness in the universal-descent hypothesis on $q$, applied over $V_2$, uniquely lifts $\delta$ and $\delta^{-1}$ to inverse arrows $\lambda:B_1\xrightarrow{\sim}B_2$.

source.place: Proposition (5.7), printed p.19: constructing the descent datum on a local realization

proof.text: The diagonal identity for $\lambda$ follows after pullback along $W_1\to V$, where it is $\beta^{-1}\beta=1$; this pullback is faithful on arrows by universal descent for $q$. On $W_3$ the cocycle is $(\beta_3^{-1}\beta_2)(\beta_2^{-1}\beta_1)=\beta_3^{-1}\beta_1$. Faithfulness over $V_3$ gives $\lambda_{23}\lambda_{12}=\lambda_{13}$. Thus $(B,\lambda)$ is a $g$-datum. Effective descent for $g$ gives $C\in\mathcal F(T)$ and a specified compatible isomorphism $\gamma:C|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. By the equation defining $\lambda$, $\beta\gamma$ on $T'\times_TV$ commutes with the canonical descent datum for the projection to $T'$.

source.place: Proposition (5.7), printed p.19: diagonal and triple-product checks, then effectivity for g

proof.text: The projection $T'\times_TV\to T'$ is a base change of $g$. Its fully faithful canonical comparison uniquely descends $\beta\gamma$ and its inverse to an isomorphism $\eta:C|_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}A$. To check that $\eta$ is a $q$-datum arrow, pull the required equation back along $T'\times_TT'\times_TV\to T'\times_TT'$. There it is precisely $\alpha\beta_1=\beta_2$ and the canonical pullback identity for $C$. This projection is again a base change of $g$, so its faithfulness gives the equation before pullback. Therefore $\eta$ realizes the original datum, proving (iii). This is arrow lifting from the assumed Hom bijections, not an unproved effectivity-locality assertion.

source.place: Proposition (5.7), printed p.19: descending the realization isomorphism and checking its compatibility

proof.text: For (i), let $X\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{b}T$ have both maps universal effective descent and put $c=ba$. First $c$ is universal descent. Indeed, for objects $C,D\in\mathcal F(T)$, a map $u:C|_X\to D|_X$ satisfying the $c$ equalizer condition also satisfies the $a$ condition, so uniquely descends to $v:C|_Y\to D|_Y$. The two pullbacks of $v$ to $Y\times_TY$ agree after pullback to $X\times_TX$ by the condition on $u$. The latter map to $Y\times_TY$ is a composite of two base changes of $a$, changing one factor at a time. Each is faithful on arrows by universal descent for $a$; hence so is their composite (injectivity composes). Thus $v$ satisfies the $b$ condition, so uniquely descends to $C\to D$. Uniqueness is successively that for $a$ and $b$. Repeating this argument after any base change proves the asserted universal full faithfulness.

source.place: Proposition (5.6), first assertion, printed p.19: Hom equalizer calculation

proof.text: Pull $c$ back along $b:Y\to T$. Its pullback is $r:X\times_TY\to Y$, second projection. The graph $s:X\to X\times_TY$, $x\mapsto(x,a(x))$, is defined by the fibre-product universal property, and $rs=a$. Since $a$ is universal effective descent, the already proved (ii) applied to $s,r$ says that $r$ is universal effective descent. This does not assume composition of effective descent maps.

source.place: Proposition (5.6), first assertion, printed p.19: refinement by the graph after base change

proof.text: Given any $c$-datum, its pullback along $b$ is effective by step 7. Step 6 gives universal descent for $c$, and $b$ is universal effective descent; thus the already proved (iii), steps 3-5, makes the datum effective with its specified realization isomorphism. Together with step 6 this proves (i). Perform the same construction after every base change to obtain the universal assertion. All comparisons used above are either the specified realization comparisons or unique lifts along fully faithful functors: identities and compositions of lifts agree because their images agree. In particular the conclusions concern actual compatible isomorphisms of data, not merely classes of objects. Identity and empty-scheme cases use the same Hom bijections and require no choice of a point or a nonempty cover.

proof_origin.place: Explicit proof by Q09 of Propositions (5.6)-(5.7), which Rydh states without proofs; direct Hom descent, refinement, base localization, then composition. No external reduction theorem assumed.
